title: The confirmatory pair: the KPSS test (a newly-authored op) agrees with ADF, bit-for-bit against statsmodels

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The ADF test rejected a unit root (the EEG is stationary), but ADF and KPSS are complementary -- ADF's null is a unit root, KPSS's null is stationarity -- and the pair is only convincing when they agree. This case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, kpssTest, completing the confirmatory pair. On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel its statistic reproduces statsmodels.tsa.stattools.kpss(regression='c') BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~7e-16); the statistic (0.20) is below the 5% critical value (0.463), so it FAILS to reject stationarity, and this AGREES with the ADF test (which rejects the unit root): the two tests concur the segment is stationary -- the strongest form of the stationarity conclusion.

claims.statement: KPSS level-stationarity statistic (lag 10) of the POz signal
KPSS fails to reject the stationarity null (statistic < critical; 1 = stationary)
ADF rejects the unit-root null (the complementary test also says stationary)
ADF and KPSS concur the segment is stationary (the confirmatory pair agrees)

validation.reference: The newly-authored kpssTest op is validated against the field-standard statsmodels.tsa.stattools.kpss(regression='c') on the identical signal. Both compute eta = N^-2 sum S_t^2 / lrv with a Bartlett long-run variance; the STATISTIC agrees BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~7e-16). The statistic (0.20) is below the 5% critical value (0.463), failing to reject stationarity, in agreement with the ADF test (which rejects the unit root).
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored kpssTest statistic reproduces statsmodels kpss bit-for-bit; (2) KPSS fails to reject stationarity AND ADF rejects the unit root -- the confirmatory pair concurs the segment is stationary. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED, adding the complement of adfTest (the confirmatory-pair partner) the ecosystem lacked; (2) the STATISTIC is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- an exact deterministic quantity given the truncation lag, so the ~7e-16 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) IMPORTANT honest caveat: as with ADF, only the statistic is bit-exact -- the KPSS critical values and p-value come from the reference tables (an approximation), so this op does NOT compute them, and the decision compares against statsmodels' tabulated 5% critical value; (4) the finding is the confirmatory-pair agreement: the KPSS statistic (0.20) is below the 5% critical value (0.463) so it FAILS to reject stationarity, and this AGREES with the ADF test (which REJECTS the unit root) -- the two complementary tests concur the eyes-closed EEG segment is stationary, the strongest form of the conclusion (ADF and KPSS can disagree, signalling near-unit-root or fractional integration; here they do not); (5) the value is a signal property; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: ADF and KPSS agreeing on stationarity is the clean case; the informative case is disagreement (ADF rejects a unit root but KPSS also rejects stationarity), which signals long memory / fractional integration -- running the pair on longer or drift-prone recordings (rest EEG with electrode movement, or HRV over hours) is where the disagreement, and a fractional-differencing follow-up, would appear. Documented, not escalated.
